author: _Gill
body:
Swearing Rule Proposal:
Excessive swearing is not permitted on anything that the Avicus Network owns or operates. The term “excessive” shall be defined by any staff member concerned with a swearing-related incident. Please use common sense and logic to determine if the swearing you would like to use is excessive or not. If unsure, please refrain from swearing.

Rule Proposal in General:
The Avicus Network has the right to ban or relinquish any player on anything owned or operated by the Avicus Network without evidence or justification. Any punishment deemed unfair by a player may be reviewed by the Senior Staff team in the “Appeals” section of our forums. Any Senior Staff decision is final.

Suggestion for TeamSpeak:
Bring back 18+ Channels with the “Description section” containing rules related to:
18+ Channel is here to talk about more sensitive issues revolving around a mature lifestyle. If you deem yourself too immature or young to take part in conversations here, you are welcome to leave. This channel does not permit the use of Racism, Harassment, or any other form of verbal abuse. This channel is still maintained under the Avicus Network, and users must still follow all rules that appear on the Avicus Website.

Please add feedback to the changes proposed above.
I will continue to add proposals that I think may be useful and constructive.

Thank you,
Max

replies.author: SnowSX3
replies.body:
The swearing rule shouldn't be defined by the staff member concerned. 

That's a bad way of enforcing rules.

There's needs to be clear rules so that everyone can follow it without difficulty.

If it was defined by the Moderator involved in the situaion, It makes it unclear and confusing for the community because they'll have to abide by all these different standards that each individual Moderator has, which again, just makes it hard to keep up and confusing.

Every the swearing rule needs to be set in stone and not altered by every staff member.

replies.author: _Gill
replies.body: No directed swearing is already a rule, so I didn't add that in. And I feel as if with the right training (as in given examples of what is excessive), then a Moderator would be able to tell what is excessive. If we just say cursing is allowed, then its going to be f*** f*** f*** and so on. Then, if the staff team says "no swearing", then the players get angry. I think leaving it allowed to an extent is a good idea, even if it means we have to trust the Mods to not abuse.
